brief.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix Q2 on track for 150T KRW combined OP; HBM shortage extends to 2027, DRAM/NAND pricing up 60-95% QoQ
brief.summary: <cite index="37-5,37-6,37-9">Samsung and SK Hynix are projected to post combined Q2 operating profit exceeding 150 trillion won, with Samsung at 88.3T won and SK Hynix at 64.3T won.</cite> <cite index="37-18,37-19,40-16">SK Hynix is on track for an operating margin approaching 80%, surpassing Q1's record 72%, driven by its 57% HBM market share commanding multi-fold margins over commodity.</cite> <cite index="40-3,40-4,40-5">Samsung regained DRAM market-share leadership at 38.6% (+2.1pp QoQ) versus SK Hynix at 28.8% (-4.1pp), with Samsung's DRAM revenue up 95.4% to $37.4B, outpacing the market's 85.3% growth.</cite> <cite index="8-3,8-13">Both companies confirmed AI-driven memory shortages extending until 2027 and beyond, with analysts noting this cycle differs as AI infrastructure consumes hardware at unprecedented rates.</cite> <cite index="12-7,12-8">TrendForce forecasts DRAM contract prices rising 58-63% QoQ in Q2 following Q1's record 90-95% surge, while NAND jumped 70-75% in Q2 after 60% in Q1.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral near-term tactical, structurally long SK Hynix. Samsung wins on DRAM volume/share recovery and commodity exposure, but SK Hynix extracts 800bp+ margin premium via HBM mix (72-80% OP margin vs. Samsung's ~66%). <cite index="43-5,43-16">Samsung passed Nvidia HBM4 qualification and secured mass-production approval, but SK Hynix retains early validation lead and larger initial allocation.</cite> <cite index="43-9,43-11,43-23">SK Hynix extended multi-year memory partnership across Nvidia's Vera CPU/Rubin GPU/RTX/Jetson platforms and remains Nvidia's largest memory partner.</cite> <cite index="40-10,40-11">Each GB of HBM consumes ~3x the wafer capacity of DDR5, tightening all DRAM segments simultaneously—benefiting Samsung's broader DRAM/server exposure but capping margin upside.</cite> Q2 numbers likely in line; watch for any Samsung HBM4 volume guidance divergence vs. SK Hynix's cemented Nvidia positioning.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="2-6,2-11">WSTS forecasts 2026 semiconductor market at ~$975B (+25% YoY), with memory segment growing 30% and reaching ~$440B; BofA defines 2026 as a supercycle similar to the 1990s, forecasting DRAM revenue +51% and NAND +45% YoY with ASPs up 33%/26%.</cite> <cite index="6-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026.</cite> <cite index="14-5,14-6,14-7">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% of global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion, prioritizing profitability over volume; analysts project price rally extending past 2028.</cite> <cite index="37-22,37-23">SK Group Chairman stated memory bottleneck expected until 2030, planning to double semiconductor capacity on a wafer basis over the next five years.</cite>

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-15,2-16">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market at $54.6B (+58% YoY); Goldman forecasts HBM demand for custom ASIC-based AI chips to surge 82%, accounting for one-third of the market.</cite> <cite index="2-24">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve ~70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="8-2,8-9,8-10">Samsung semiconductor division posted 53.7T won ($36.1B) Q1 OP, ~94% of total; SK Hynix posted record Q1 revenue of 52.6T won ($35.5B) and OP of 37.6T won ($27.8B), largely HBM-fueled.</cite> <cite index="2-18,2-19">HBM3E remains flagship in 2026, with Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Google, and AWS selecting HBM3E for proprietary ASICs.</cite> <cite index="5-3,5-4,5-5,5-6">Industry exploring separating HBM from GPUs via optical links to expand capacity several-fold beyond current architectures, per Korean memory manufacturer researchers.</cite> Supply remains sold out through 2027; customers reserving years ahead.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix Q2 consensus: 150T won combined OP, margins at record highs
news_pulse.implication: Samsung Q2 OP est. 88.3T won (66% margin); SK Hynix 64.3T won (approaching 80% margin). Memory division driving 95% of Samsung profit. TSMC Q2 margin projected 56.5-58.5%, widening gap vs. memory peers.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix secures multi-year Nvidia Vera CPU/Rubin GPU memory partnership; remains largest partner
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix to supply HBM4 for Rubin, LPDDR5X for Vera CPU (1.2TB/s, <30W vs. DDR5's >100W). Samsung passed HBM4 qual but SK Hynix holds early allocation lead. Multi-vendor strategy persists (Samsung/Micron also qualified).

news_pulse.headline: Samsung regains DRAM share crown at 38.6%, SK Hynix falls to 28.8% despite record margins
news_pulse.implication: Samsung DRAM revenue $37.4B (+95.4%), outpacing market's 85.3% growth. SK Hynix 72% Q1 margin (record) vs. Samsung ~66%. HBM consumes 3x wafer capacity of DDR5, tightening all segments. Samsung wins volume, SK Hynix wins profitability.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler AI capex revised to $725B in 2026, up from $670B pre-Q1 earnings
news_pulse.implication: Meta raised 2026 capex to $125-145B (up $10B both ends) citing higher component pricing. Amazon reaffirmed $200B, Microsoft ~$190B, Alphabet $175-185B. Meta stock -6% on increased forecast. Component pricing pressure confirmed.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity scaling to 130K wpm by end-2026; Nvidia holds 60%+ allocation
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS capacity doubling from ~35K wpm (late 2024) to 130K wpm (end-2026). Nvidia secures 60-70% of total capacity for Blackwell/Rubin. TSMC outsourcing 240-270K wafers annually to Amkor/SPIL. Packaging remains critical bottleneck.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q2 contract prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% following Q1's record 90-95% and 60% surges
news_pulse.implication: Q1 saw DRAM contracts +90-95%, NAND +55-60%. Q2 acceleration in NAND (70-75%) outpaces DRAM (58-63%) for first time. Enterprise SSD demand absorbing NAND; new fab capacity not until late 2027. LPDDR prices steepest increases in history.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix rebound +5.4%/+10.6% after Monday's 10%/8% rout; KOSPI circuit breaker triggered
news_pulse.implication: KOSPI plunged >8% June 8, triggering Level 1 circuit breaker (20-min halt) on semi selloff and rate-hike fears. Samsung -10.2% Monday, SK Hynix -8%. Tuesday rebound on bargain buying and SK Hynix-Nvidia partnership news. Vol spike underscores momentum fragility.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Chairman: Memory bottleneck to persist until 2030; plans to double wafer capacity in 5 years
news_pulse.implication: SK Group Chairman Choi at Computex 2026 confirmed structural shortage extending through decade. Doubling capacity on wafer basis by 2031 implies disciplined ramp vs. demand trajectory. Supports extended pricing power thesis.

brief.derivatives_signal: No ADR/futures pricing in payload. Implied vol likely elevated post-Monday circuit breaker. KOSPI 200 futures and options positioning skewed put-heavy near-term given 8%+ drawdown, but structural HBM supply lock and 150T won Q2 OP consensus argue for dip-buying into results. Watch USD/KRW for export FX sensitivity (stronger won = margin headwind). Options market pricing binary risk around any Samsung HBM4 volume guidance vs. SK Hynix Nvidia allocation clarity.
watch_for_next_3h: Any revised Samsung/SK Hynix Q2 guidance or early July prelim announcements (typically first week of July for Korean semis)
Further hyperscaler (Meta/MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL) commentary on component cost inflation and memory allocation constraints post-earnings
TSMC June revenue report (due ~July 10) for CoWoS utilization proxy and any capacity allocation shifts between Nvidia/AMD/Google
Korean government semiconductor investment incentive announcements tied to regional fab expansion (Chungcheong/Honam rumors circulating)
Any DRAM/NAND spot price divergence from contract pricing (TrendForce noted mid-April spot softness vs. contract strength)
